content: WikiDoc provides a reference management system that allows users to insert references using their PubMed ID numbers. This system ensures that references are automatically numbered and move along with the text when it is relocated. All references are inserted at the bottom of the article, and clicking on a reference takes the user directly to the cited article. This process is designed to be simple and efficient. To cite references in WikiDoc, users typically insert a number in the text, such as (1) or 1, which corresponds to a reference listed at the end of the article. However, this manual method is not the preferred approach in WikiDoc. Instead, WikiDoc features an automated reference manager with several advantages: references are automatically numbered, they move with the text, and they provide clickable links to the original articles. Unlike the traditional method of typing references at the end of the article, the WikiDoc reference manager allows users to insert code for the reference directly after the relevant material. This is done using a software program that generates the necessary code. The following steps outline how to use the WikiDoc reference manager: 1. Use PubMed to locate the desired article. 2. Copy the PubMed ID (PMID) number, which is typically found at the bottom of the article's abstract. For example, a PMID might look like this: PMID: 19032997. 3. Paste the PMID into a software program that generates Wiki language code for the reference. Several tools are available for this purpose, such as: SUMSearch Biomedical Citation Maker DOI Wikipedia reference generator DTU Informatics PMID to Cite journal OttoBib for ISBNs Dave's Template Filler for various IDs (e.g., DrugBank, HGNC, PubMed, PubChem, URLs). 4. Ensure the add ref tag option is selected in the reference manager. 5. Submit the information to generate the Wiki language code. 6. Copy the generated Wiki language code. For example, the output for PMID 19032997 might look like this: ``` {{cite journal | author = Gibson CM, Pride YB, Frederick PD, et al. | title = Trends in reperfusion strategies, door-to-needle and door-to-balloon times, and in-hospital mortality among patients with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction enrolled in the National Registry of Myocardial Infarction from 1990 to 2006 | journal = Am. Heart J. | url = }} ``` 7. Paste this code into the text where the superscript number for the reference should appear. For instance: ``` Gibson et al. recently summarized the improvements made in clinical outcomes as a result of 15 years of quality improvement efforts in the NRMI registry {{cite journal | author = Gibson CM, Pride YB, Frederick PD, et al. | title = Trends in reperfusion strategies, door-to-needle and door-to-balloon times, and in-hospital mortality among patients with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction enrolled in the National Registry of Myocardial Infarction from 1990 to 2006 | journal = Am. Heart J. | url = }}. ``` This would generate text like: ``` Gibson et al. recently summarized the improvements made in clinical outcomes as a result of 15 years of quality improvement efforts in the NRMI registry. ↑ Gibson CM, Pride YB, Frederick PD, et al. (2008). Trends in reperfusion strategies, door-to-needle and door-to-balloon times, and in-hospital mortality among patients with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction enrolled in the National Registry of Myocardial Infarction from 1990 to 2006. Am. Heart J. 156(6): 1035–44. PMID 19032997. ``` If users prefer not to use the reference manager, they can manually type references. To do this: 1. Insert `<ref>` tags immediately after the sentence where the footnote number should appear. 2. Type the reference text between the `<ref>` tags. For example: ``` <ref>Author Name, Title of the Article, Journal Name, Year, Volume, Page Numbers.</ref> ``` If the same reference is used multiple times, assign a name to the reference using the `name` attribute to avoid duplication. To display references at the bottom of the article, include the following code: ``` <references /> ``` This will generate a reference list in small font, formatted in two columns, with links to the original articles and abstracts. The output will look like this: ``` ↑ J Fam Pract. 2000 Oct;49(10):921-3. ```
